task.name: A model declared not dev-capable is still selected for dev by the adaptive router
task.story_text:
## Observed

An operator declared two models ineligible to own the dev role and the adaptive
router assigned dev to one of them anyway, on the next sprint, from a
configuration snapshot that contained the declaration.

`forge.yaml` overlaid the shipped catalog entry:

```yaml
    - provider: google
      model: gemini-3.5-flash
      transport: {kind: api}
      routing:
        dev_capable: false
```

The declaration resolved, and config load reported it:

```
forge.yaml declares google/gemini-3.5-flash/api, which the shipped catalog also
defines, and the two resolve to different routing (dev_capable: forge.yaml=False
builtin=True). Removing the declaration would change model selection.
```

The declaration was committed at 17:25:35. The sprint logged `Sprint config
pinned` at 17:30:31, and that pinned snapshot carries the declaration at line 125.

Sprint `a0b5fc18626b` then dispatched dev to that model for two stories. The
recorded routing decision lists it as an admitted candidate with no exclusion:

```
base_tier_from_score: mid
selected:  google-gemini-3.5-flash-api
candidate_pool:
   True   openai-gpt-5.6-terra-cli            reason: none
   True   google-gemini-3.5-flash-api         reason: none     ← selected
   True   google-gemini-3.1-pro-preview-api   reason: none
   False  anthropic-opus-cli                  reason: tier_mismatch
   False  (five others)                       reason: tier_mismatch
```

`reason: none` is the value recorded for a candidate with nothing against it. The
pool has a vocabulary for exclusions — `tier_mismatch` appears six times in the
same record — and no entry anywhere in it refers to dev capability.

Removing the entries from `models.enabled` outright did take effect: the
adaptive pool then reported seven models with neither Google entry present.

## Expected

A declared routing constraint binds every path that selects a model. Where an
operator states that a model may not own a role, no mechanism assigns that role
to it — the declaration is a statement about what the system is permitted to do,
not a hint one selection strategy may weigh and another may honour. A constraint
that holds only on the path the run does not take has no effect at all.

Two selection paths over one configuration must not disagree about eligibility.
They may legitimately differ on preference — which admitted candidate is best is
exactly what an adaptive layer is for — but the set of candidates a configuration
admits is the same set either way, and a model excluded by declaration is absent
from both.

This is load-bearing beyond its own scope. Declaring a model ineligible for a
role is the operator's remedy when a model or a path is discovered to be unsafe
mid-flight; a remedy that silently fails leaves no way to contain a fault except
deleting the model from the configuration entirely, which also surrenders every
role it was performing correctly.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `d91f9ccf647d7f3a63e7f44dcf0889168e7822b6` captured at `2026-09-06T05:53:00.429115+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `forge.yaml` — `sha256:3d699e1911ad6e8664625536ea81456d844e33d5a3de0534bf5d9c86ba242e86`
- `src/theforge/config/role_derivation.py` — `sha256:1c20e810d587b67ef57d9a491bbd41c4844044c85cd87e13797aa30fd5a3116a`
- `src/theforge/config/model_catalog.py` — `sha256:162b1689d03f20e50a9b11c90b5267fe36c4980c01efa757071761fc26fff659`
- `src/theforge/config/models.py` — `sha256:e55f3549db704cbebecf1f82e823c150ab846e05f935130361f00ef0aa47fb61`
- `src/theforge/config/profiles.py` — `sha256:014285ed2c2e9516fb762566b111a3c61f3cd50794879cfa219a33ba3e6ca7c6`
- `src/theforge/config/load.py` — `sha256:6a8032a47a9681d73754ce6a068f3c3e799e427a0d3d97e0fd82d4d1344132c8`
- `src/theforge/assignment.py` — `sha256:7f51b053f63685ad3046b3c0a9c35598d88ea21f0f114b094651b34462bcfa2f`
- `docs/guides/adaptive-assignment.md` — `sha256:5f21cc3992bbd4a931279e60005c643c079a6c829d894186efecdc73c9b66c71`
- `.forge/logs/issues-2919,2920,2921,2922,2923/run-a0b5fc18626b.log` — `sha256:0a046e82130de3836641b7d28e7a86b4f3f2870f53859e6a6ff64e5313df37a8`

### Observed symptom

A model declared `routing.dev_capable: false` in forge.yaml (overlaying a
shipped catalog entry that declares it `true`) is still selected for the dev
role by the adaptive router. The recorded routing_decision for sprint
a0b5fc18626b lists google-gemini-3.5-flash-api in the dev candidate_pool as
`included: true, reason: none` — the same "nothing against it" value used for
every legitimately eligible candidate — and it was subsequently dispatched to
dev on two stories (#2919, #2920).

### Reproduction / evidence

- forge.yaml overlay: `models: ...  - provider: google, model: gemini-3.5-flash,
  transport: {kind: api}, routing: {dev_capable: false}` (config load logged
  the declaration and its conflict with the builtin catalog value, confirming
  it resolved to dev_capable=False in the effective config).
- Sprint config pinned at 17:30:31 carries the declaration (line 125 of the
  pinned snapshot, per the issue body).
- .forge/logs/issues-2919,2920,2921,2922,2923/run-a0b5fc18626b.log shows
  google-gemini-3.5-flash-api actually running dev iterations for issue-2919
  and issue-2920.
- The routing_decision candidate_pool (issue body) shows
  `True   google-gemini-3.5-flash-api   reason: none` with no dev-capability
  exclusion reason anywhere in the pool's vocabulary (only `tier_mismatch`
  appears, 6 times, for unrelated tier mismatches).

### Hypotheses tested

- **[ruled out]** The static role_derivation.py dev-selection path ignores dev_capable and that is what dispatched the model.
  - Evidence: src/theforge/config/role_derivation.py:279 explicitly filters `dev_candidates = [(k, i) for k, i in dev_pool if i.dev_capable]` before falling back to the unfiltered pool only when nothing is dev_capable. This path DOES honor the flag. The observed run instead produced an adaptive routing_decision (tier-scored candidate_pool with per-candidate `reason` fields, base_tier_from_score, an admitted 9-candidate pool with tier_mismatch exclusions) — the shape produced by assign_models() in src/theforge/assignment.py, not by derive_roles().
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Read directly from the current repository source.
- **[confirmed]** The adaptive assignment path (assign_models() in assignment.py) never receives the declared dev_capable flag because the AgentDef pool objects it operates on do not carry that field, so no eligibility filter in that path can act on it.
  - Evidence: 1. `AgentDef` (src/theforge/config/models.py:133-162) has no `dev_capable`
   field. Its fields are name/provider/model/budget/timeout/tier/cli/
   api_fallback/strengths/transport/base_url/registry_id/registry_source/
   pricing fields/reasoning_mode — dev_capable is absent.
2. `_agents_from_models()` (src/theforge/config/profiles.py:92-133), the
   function that builds the AgentDef pool feeding assign_models() from the
   `models:` list, explicitly copies many ModelInfo fields onto each
   AgentDef (provider, model, tier, cli, transport, base_url, registry_id,
   registry_source, pricing fields, reasoning_mode) but does not copy
   `info.dev_capable`. It is silently dropped at construction.
3. This pool is exactly what feeds the adaptive router: config/load.py:1554
   calls `_agents_from_models(models, budget_usd_val, registry=model_registry)`.
4. `grep dev_capable src/theforge/assignment.py` returns zero matches —
   no eligibility function in the adaptive router (`_pick_agent`,
   `_agents_by_tier`, `_capability_pool`, `_capability_exclusions`,
   `_auth_reason`, `_single_model_pool`) ever reads or checks it.
5. The only capability-exclusion mechanism assignment.py has
   (`ROLE_REQUIRED_CAPABILITY`, #2466) maps `advisor`/`planner`/
   `plan_review`/`code_review` to a *probed, demonstrated-absence*
   capability record — "dev" is not a key in that dict, and even where it
   is used, it is not driven by the declared `routing.dev_capable` config
   field at all; it is driven by a separate probe-result substrate.
6. `_pick_agent()`'s dev-role candidate list (assignment.py:949, `[a for a
   in _agents_by_tier(agents, tier) if _has_auth(a, secrets)]`) filters
   only by tier and auth, then reranks by profile signals — there is no
   step that could exclude a tier-matched, authenticated AgentDef for
   being declared dev-incapable, because that information was never
   attached to the AgentDef in the first place.
This exactly matches the observed candidate_pool: the model is
tier-matched (mid, alongside the other admitted mid/strong candidates)
and authenticated, so it is admitted with `reason: none`, and no
exclusion reason for dev-incapability exists in the vocabulary because
the mechanism that would produce one was never wired to this data path.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All claims verified against current repository source, not against any prior assertion or attached log alone.

### Confirmed cause

The adaptive router's candidate representation (`AgentDef`, defined in
src/theforge/config/models.py) has no field for the declared `routing.dev_capable`
eligibility flag, and the function that builds the `AgentDef` pool consumed by
`assign_models()` — `_agents_from_models()` in src/theforge/config/profiles.py —
does not copy `ModelInfo.dev_capable` onto the `AgentDef` it constructs. As a
result, `assign_models()`'s dev-role selection (`_pick_agent`, filtering only
by tier and auth) has no way to see or enforce the declaration at all, so a
model declared dev-incapable is treated identically to one that was never
restricted and is admitted to the pool with `reason: none`. This is a data-loss
bug at pool construction, not a missing conditional in the selection logic
itself — the selection logic has nothing to condition on because the field
never survives the AgentDef conversion.

Support: Read directly from source: src/theforge/config/models.py:133-162 (AgentDef
dataclass field list — no dev_capable), src/theforge/config/profiles.py:92-133
(_agents_from_models field-copy list, dev_capable omitted), src/theforge/config/load.py:1554
(call site feeding the adaptive router), and an exhaustive grep of
src/theforge/assignment.py for "dev_capable" (zero matches). This is original
analysis from this investigation, not a restatement of a prior assertion —
the issue body itself stops at "no diagnosis yet."
Support provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All cited files were read directly during this investigation; none of this mechanism was previously documented or asserted elsewhere in the repo (docs/guides/adaptive-assignment.md describes dev_capable's sibling static-vs-adaptive boundary only in general terms, not this specific gap).

### Affected code path

src/theforge/config/models.py:133 (AgentDef dataclass — missing dev_capable field);
src/theforge/config/profiles.py:92-133 (_agents_from_models — drops
info.dev_capable when constructing AgentDef); src/theforge/assignment.py
(dev-role eligibility/selection — _pick_agent at line 909, _agents_by_tier,
_single_model_pool at line 1995 — has no dev_capable-aware exclusion branch
because the data never arrives).

### Fix-success criterion

Given a `models:` entry whose effective (post-overlay) `routing.dev_capable`
resolves to false, a sprint run's dev-role routing_decision.candidate_pool
must list that model as `included: false` with a canonical exclusion reason
distinct from `tier_mismatch` (e.g. a `dev_incapable`-style reason), and
`assign_models()` must never select it for the dev role — mirroring the
guarantee role_derivation.py:279 already provides on the static path — for
both a story that starts fresh and one resumed from a pinned config snapshot
containing the declaration.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- Operators get no signal at declaration time that dev_capable: false will be silently unenforced on the adaptive path — config load only reports that the declaration resolved and would 'change model selection,' which is misleading for the path this issue exercises. (related: #2926 (explicitly noted as out of scope by the issue body itself))

### Advisory repair proposal

> Advisory only: this is an unverified repair idea from the investigation, not part of the confirmed diagnosis contract.

Add a `dev_capable: bool = True` field to `AgentDef`, populate it from
`info.dev_capable` in `_agents_from_models()`, and add a dev-role exclusion
check (parallel to `_capability_pool`/`_single_model_pool`'s existing
reason-vocabulary pattern) that marks `included: false` with a new reason
constant when `dev_capable` is false, consulted wherever `_pick_agent`/
`_agents_by_tier` build the dev candidate list. This investigation did not
verify all call sites that would need the new field threaded through (e.g.
whether other adaptive mechanisms like post-plan demotion at
assignment.py:3230 need the same guard) — that should be checked from the
same `_agents_from_models` construction point outward.

### Notes

Out of scope per the issue: the missing operator-facing signal that the
declaration was inert at declaration time. That is a separate reporting gap
(config load only validates that the declaration *resolved*, not that some
consumer will *enforce* it) and may share a cause or may not — not
investigated here.

claims.claim: When phase names are validated from a hand-maintained list instead of deriving from actual dispatch sites, the newest dispatched phase becomes unnameable in routing.phase_eligibility until a separate source edit adds it.

Fixing phase-vocabulary drift exposed a second coupling in knowledge-summary selection: preserving the plan-derived profile matters because fallback transport, budget, timeout, and role identity can be lost if agent-pool selection overrides it.
Guard tests against future phase drift are themselves prone to drift when they enumerate a fixed set of source files or apply incomplete literal-detection rules.
Validation messaging for operator-named phases must distinguish unrecognized phases from deliberately closed ones, or the loader can suggest a remediation it will not actually accept.
Helper APIs added during a registry refactor can remain disconnected unless call sites or tests are updated to exercise them directly.

correspondences.description: An explicit dev pin to a model declared dev_capable=false is still honored as the dev owner and the routing candidate pool marks that model included with reason none.

When every adaptive dev candidate is declared dev_capable=false, assign_models raises a plain ValueError, while the structurally identical refusal for a demonstrated-absent capability raises the typed NoCapableCandidateError one block earlier.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Plan risk 1 (explicit dev profile override pinned to a dev_capable:false model) is carried, not retired. assignment.py:3693-3699 short-circuits the pool entirely for 'dev' in explicit_profiles — rationale is set and no candidate pool is consulted — so a dev_capable filter on role_pools['dev'] cannot reach it. The plan's mitigation defers the decision to the dev agent rather than settling it. This does not threaten the acceptance criteria (all three target the adaptive models.enabled path exercised by the reported run), which is why it is P1-impl rather than P1.
  Suggestion: Mirror the existing precedent one line down: _explicit_capability_warning(dev_profile, 'dev', capability_records) already annotates the rationale when an explicit pin contradicts a capability record. Do the same for dev_capable (a rationale warning, not a hard refusal — the explicit-override contract elsewhere honors the operator pin), and note the fail-closed question as a follow-up issue rather than changing override semantics in this story.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Plan risk 2 (fallback/exploration/post-plan/budget paths reseating a dev-incapable model) is retired for the in-run paths (all of assignment.py:3701/3757/3801/3815/3835/3849 consume dev_pool, and 4221 passes role_pools), but the post-plan checkpoint at assignment.py:3230 rebuilds its own pool via _capability_pool(agents, _capability_exclusions(agents, 'dev', ...)) from the raw agents list and will not inherit the filter automatically. The plan names this path and adds a test for it, so it is covered — flagged only so the dev does not assume role_pools threading suffices. Risk 3 (reason precedence hiding the declaration behind tier_mismatch) is retired by Step 2's explicit ordering requirement, which is implementable given _single_model_pool's deterministic elif chain.
  Suggestion: Apply the dev_capable filter at assignment.py:3230 as a separate explicit step alongside the existing capability filter, and place the new reason branch after the selected-name/locked checks but before the a.tier != target_tier check at assignment.py:2023.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Preserve `routing.dev_capable` through the `ModelInfo` to `AgentDef` conversion, then make the adaptive dev-role pool treat `dev_capable: false` as a hard eligibility exclusion before ranking, fallback, exploration, post-plan demotion, or budget downgrade can pick it. Record the exclusion with a new canonical reason so the routing decision explains the same hard constraint it enforces.

steps.description: Thread declared dev capability into the adaptive agent pool.
steps.details: Add a defaulted `dev_capable: bool = True` field to `AgentDef` without breaking existing positional test construction, and copy `info.dev_capable` in `_agents_from_models()`. Add a focused config test proving a `models.enabled` inline overlay with `routing.dev_capable: false` loads into `config.agents` with `agent.dev_capable is False`.

steps.description: Apply dev-capability as a hard adaptive eligibility rule and audit reason.
steps.details: Add a canonical exclusion reason such as `REASON_DEV_INCAPABLE = "dev_incapable"` to `EXCLUSION_REASONS` and the explain renderer. Filter dev-role candidates using the existing `role` argument in `_pick_agent`, build `role_pools["dev"]` from agents that remain after capability exclusions and `dev_capable` filtering, and pass that pool through existing dev selection, fallback, exploration, post-plan checkpoint, and `_enforce_budget(role_pools=...)` paths. Make the dev `candidate_pool` renderer mark every non-selected `dev_capable is False` agent as `included: false` with the new reason before tier or auth exclusions can hide the declaration; fail closed instead of selecting when no non-explicit dev-capable candidate remains.

steps.description: Lock the behavior with seam-level regression coverage.
steps.details: Add an assignment-level test where an authenticated same-tier `AgentDef(dev_capable=False)` is not selected for dev and appears in `routing_decision["dev"]["candidate_pool"]` as `included: false, reason: dev_incapable`. Add a load-to-assign seam test for both a normal temp `forge.yaml` and the same contents loaded from a sprint-style pinned path, proving a `models.enabled` overlay survives config load and produces the same exclusion. Add a post-plan checkpoint regression showing a reduced-tier dev candidate with `dev_capable=False` is not used for demotion.

criteria_mapping.criterion: Given a `models:` entry whose effective (post-overlay) `routing.dev_capable` resolves to false, a sprint run's dev-role routing_decision.candidate_pool must list that model as `included: false` with a canonical exclusion reason distinct from `tier_mismatch`.
`assign_models()` must never select a `routing.dev_capable: false` model for the dev role.
The guarantee must hold for both a story that starts fresh and one resumed from a pinned config snapshot containing the declaration.

risks.description: The spec prose could be read to include explicit `dev` overrides, while the observed failure and fix-success criterion target adaptive selection from `models.enabled`.
risks.mitigation: Treat resolvable explicit dev pins to a `dev_capable: false` agent as fail-closed unless existing config tests prove that explicit contradictory override is an intentional separate contract; otherwise document it as a follow-up rather than silently honoring it.

risks.description: Filtering only the first `_pick_agent()` call would still allow fallback, exploration, post-plan demotion, or budget downgrade to reseat a dev-incapable model.
risks.mitigation: Derive one dev-eligible role pool and use it everywhere existing dev paths already consume `role_pools` or `dev_pool`; the tests must include at least normal assignment and post-plan demotion.

risks.description: Reason precedence can hide the operator declaration behind `tier_mismatch` or auth failures.
risks.mitigation: For the dev candidate-pool audit, report `dev_incapable` before tier/auth exclusions so the hard declaration remains visible and machine-queryable.
